infra-context

Infra map

How the system under test (tuDeclaracion.com) is built, run and deployed, and the budgets it must hold. Phase 2 (architecture) sections; Phase 3 adds backend, frontend, environments and CI/CD.

Overview

tuDeclaracion is a single-repository, full-stack web application for Uruguayan accountants: it turns an accounting TXT export into the PADI file that DGI accepts for the VAT forms 2181 and 1376. The pattern is a Next.js 15 App Router monolith whose domain logic lives in pure TypeScript modules (src/modules/), with Supabase as the whole backend (Postgres with Row Level Security, Auth, one Edge Function). Most reads and writes go from the browser straight to Supabase and are guarded by RLS; only four Server Actions and two route handlers run application code on the server. There is no ORM, no public REST API and no OpenAPI spec.

The SRS (.context/SRS/02-system-architecture.md) plans validator, forms, domain, services and shared folders; none exist in the code. The code is what the table above shows.

Containers and data flow

  • Browser to Next.js (HTTPS): page loads. middleware.ts runs first on every request except static assets and images.
  • Browser to Supabase Auth: signup, login, Google OAuth start, forgot and reset password are called from client components with supabase-js (signUp, signInWithPassword, signInWithOAuth, resetPasswordForEmail, updateUser). The server is not in that path.
  • Browser to Postgres (REST and RPC): the dashboard, company, plan-de-cuentas and mapping screens read and write tables and call RPCs from the browser client (for example insertar_asientos, borrar_periodo, guardar_mapeo_1376, crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas). Authorization is RLS plus security invoker RPCs.
  • Next.js to Supabase Auth: auth.getUser() in middleware and Server Components, verifyOtp in /auth/confirm, exchangeCodeForSession in /auth/callback, signOut in salir.
  • Next.js to Postgres: Server Components query with the cookie-scoped server client (RLS applies). Only the BCU rate cache is written with the admin client (secret key, bypasses RLS).
  • Next.js to BCU: SOAP POST from modules/cotizacion/fetch-cotizacion-bcu.ts, run on the server because the BCU service does not allow browser CORS.
  • Auth to send-email to Resend: every Auth email (signup confirmation, recovery) goes through the Send Email hook to the Edge Function, which verifies the webhook signature and sends through Resend (ADR-0002).
  • In-browser computation: the TXT is parsed and normalized in the browser (parse-asientos, normalize-asiento, imported by the client import dialog) and stored through one RPC; the PADI text file is generated in the browser and downloaded as a Blob (generate-padi-file*.ts imported by client components). Consolidation per declaration line (tax-engine/consolidate-lines) and the 1376 totals run in the Server Component of the declaration pages.
  • Cloudflare Turnstile: not drawn. Login, signup and forgot-password load challenges.cloudflare.com in the browser and pass the token as captchaToken to Supabase Auth, which verifies it (provider setting lives in the Supabase dashboard, not in the repo).

Auth flow

Session mechanism: Supabase Auth with the PKCE flow; the session lives in sb-* cookies managed by @supabase/ssr. Cookie options: secure in production, httpOnly false on purpose (the browser client reads document.cookie), path /, SameSite Lax.

Email and password signup

  1. /signup (client page) calls supabase.auth.signUp with emailRedirectTo = ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/auth/confirm?next=/inicio, the Turnstile captchaToken and optional metadata plan_elegido. Client rule: password of at least 10 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a digit.
  2. Supabase creates the auth.users row; trigger on_auth_user_created runs handle_new_user() (security definer) and inserts the tenant row public.cuenta (id, email).
  3. Supabase calls the Send Email hook; send-email verifies the Standard Webhooks signature (401 on failure) and sends a link of the form {site_url}/auth/confirm?token_hash=...&type=...&redirect_to=... through Resend.
  4. The user opens the link: GET /auth/confirm calls verifyOtp({ type, token_hash }), sets the session cookies and redirects to safeInternalPath(next, '/inicio'). On failure it redirects to /login?error=verification-failed, or to /forgot-password?error=expired when type=recovery.
  5. A duplicate email is detected from Supabase's anti-enumeration response (empty identities) and shown as "Este correo ya esta registrado".

Login, session and route gating

  1. /login calls signInWithPassword from the browser (with captchaToken). Error codes invalid_credentials, email_not_confirmed, captcha_failed and over_request_rate_limit map to fixed Spanish messages. Success: router.push('/inicio') and router.refresh(). The ?redirect= parameter that middleware adds is never read by the login page.
  2. Middleware refreshes the session on each request with supabase.auth.getUser() (token revalidated against Supabase, not the local cookie). Protected prefixes /inicio, /cuenta, /empresas, /dashboard redirect anonymous users to /login?redirect=<path>. Authenticated users hitting /login, /signup or /forgot-password are redirected to /inicio. /reset-password and /auth/* are intentionally not gated.

Google OAuth

  1. GoogleSignInButton calls signInWithOAuth({ provider: 'google', redirectTo: ${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}/auth/callback }).
  2. GET /auth/callback runs exchangeCodeForSession(code), fills cuenta.nombre from the Google profile only when it is empty, and redirects to safeInternalPath(next, '/inicio'). A provider denial or failed exchange goes to /login?error=google-auth-failed. Identity linking by verified email is Supabase's default (ADR-0004 in the product repo).

Password recovery and sign-out

  1. /forgot-password calls resetPasswordForEmail with redirectTo = .../auth/confirm?type=recovery&next=/reset-password; the email arrives through the same hook; /auth/confirm verifies the OTP; /reset-password checks the recovery session and calls updateUser({ password }).
  2. Sign-out is the Server Action salir(): signOut(), delete the empresa_activa_id cookie, redirect('/login'). A sign-out error is logged but never blocks the redirect.
  3. Active company: Server Action seleccionarEmpresaActiva sets empresa_activa_id (httpOnly, SameSite Lax, secure in production, 30 days). resolverEmpresaActiva trusts it only if RLS returns that company, else falls back to the most recently created one.

Database at architecture level

One Supabase PostgreSQL database, accessed only through supabase-js (PostgREST) and five RPCs; there is no ORM. Subsystems: tenancy (cuenta, empresa), chart of accounts (codigo_iva, plan_cuentas), accounting entries and declarations (asiento, declaracion, declaracion_1376), form 1376 mapping (codigo_linea_1376, mapeo_1376) and the shared BCU rate cache (cotizacion_bcu_cache). All ten tables have RLS enabled. Tenant isolation root: empresa.cuenta_id = (select auth.uid()); child tables scope through a join to empresa. Reference tables (codigo_iva, codigo_linea_1376) and the BCU cache are readable by any authenticated user and not tenant-scoped. RPCs: insertar_asientos, crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, guardar_mapeo_1376, borrar_periodo, all security invoker so RLS applies; the only security definer function is the trigger handle_new_user(). Tables, columns, relationships and state machines belong to business-data-context (bun run context:map business-data-context); they are not restated here. The live database was not inspected (dbhub not connected); the schema above comes from the migrations.

Security architecture

  • AuthN: Supabase Auth (email and password, Google OAuth, email confirmation, Turnstile CAPTCHA), cookie session, middleware revalidation.
  • AuthZ: a single role (one user is one cuenta, no multiple roles in the MVP); data access is decided by RLS, not by application code.
  • Privileged access: the secret key is read only in src/infrastructure/supabase/admin.ts and used only for the BCU cache; the two cache Server Actions re-check the session themselves because RLS no longer stops an anonymous caller.
  • Data protection and headers: see nfr-security. Password storage and session lifetime are Supabase Auth's; they are not configured in the repo.

Performance hooks

No application caching is declared (no revalidate, unstable_cache or fetch cache options in src/). The only cache is the table cotizacion_bcu_cache. No rate limiting in the app layer; see nfr-performance and nfr-security.

Architecture decision records

Product ADRs (in the app repo, ../tudeclaracion/.context/ADR/) that shape this architecture: ADR-0001 modular reusable tax platform, ADR-0002 auth email through the Send Email hook and Resend, ADR-0003 declaration-period entity, ADR-0004 Google OAuth with automatic identity linking, ADR-0005 configurable TXT field layout for 2181, ADR-0006 1376 aggregation by account, ADR-0007 chart of accounts per declaration, ADR-0008 RUT required only for 2181 lines, ADR-0009 1376 reads columns by header, ADR-0010 1376 uses both 2181 criteria. No test-architecture ADR was written in this phase: none of the candidates passed both gates (see discovery-gaps).

QA relevance

  • Most behavior is reachable only through the UI and Supabase calls made by the browser; there is no public REST API to test directly.
  • Components worth separate test focus: auth flows and middleware gating, tenant isolation (RLS, two accounts), TXT import and RPC rules, PADI file output, BCU rate fallback.
  • Environment needs: Supabase project variables NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY; SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY for the BCU cache; NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL for email and OAuth redirects; optional NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY.
  • Automation blockers to plan for: Turnstile CAPTCHA, email confirmation delivered through Resend, Google OAuth redirects, and no seed users (cuenta.id is a foreign key to auth.users).

Failure modes a test must account for. Email delivery: signup and recovery depend on the hook and Resend; with the sandbox sender, delivery is limited to the Resend account owner until a domain is verified (ADR-0002), so a test inbox may never receive the link. BCU: the call has no timeout or retry; on any failure the app falls back to the cached row and shows state fallback or error (resolverCotizacionBcu), and the import action returns { ok: false }. Turnstile: when the site key is set but the widget script is blocked, the submit button stays disabled (captchaReady); when the key is unset the forms submit without a token, which only works while CAPTCHA is off in Supabase. Sentry and analytics: none declared (no such package in package.json).

Not present, stated without pass/fail framing: no full CSP (script-src, connect-src), no application-layer rate limiting (login, signup and recovery call Supabase Auth directly from the browser, so limits live in Supabase), no sanitize/DOMPurify-style package (the threat model records no dangerouslySetInnerHTML in src/), no CI dependency audit. A pattern search of src/, supabase/, middleware.ts, next.config.ts and render.yaml found no hard-coded secrets. The threat model (.context/security/threat-model.md, 2026-09-22 with updates to 2026-10-18) is the product team's own review; its resolved items match the code read here. QA relevance: open-redirect, route-gating and two-account isolation checks are testable end to end; the OWASP ZAP baseline against staging is possible; hosted Auth settings need a dashboard check.

Backend

There is no separate API server. The backend is three Server Actions files, two route handlers, the session middleware and Supabase (Postgres with RLS, Auth, one Deno Edge Function), all inside the one Next.js app. Business logic lives in pure modules under src/modules/. The request sequence and trust boundaries are in the architecture section; this section holds the facts a test setup needs.

Database, migrations and RPCs

  • Migrations: 27 SQL files in supabase/migrations/, from 20260712000000_baseline_cuenta_empresa.sql to 20261110103201_asiento_tipo_alfabetico.sql. There is no supabase/seed.sql although config.toml points at one.
  • How they are applied: .context/backend-setup.md says the project uses the Supabase MCP and no local Supabase CLI. No script in package.json applies migrations and no CI does either; the path to the hosted database is not documented beyond that.
  • RPCs called from the app (5, all security invoker, so RLS applies): insertar_asientos (redefined 4 times, latest in 20261017120000_limitar_tamano_payload_rpcs.sql), crear_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, editar_empresa_con_plan_cuentas, guardar_mapeo_1376, borrar_periodo (20261014120000). Each one matches a .rpc('...') call in src/.
  • Other functions (not callable RPCs): set_updated_at() trigger function and handle_new_user() (security definer, creates the cuenta row when Auth inserts a user; EXECUTE restricted per backend-setup.md).
  • Tenancy: RLS on business tables scoped through cuenta_id = (select auth.uid()), directly or through empresa. cotizacion_bcu_cache is read-only for users and written by the admin client.
  • Health check: none (no /api/health or equivalent route).

Local development setup

git clone https://github.com/jpl1899/tudeclaracion.git
cd tudeclaracion
bun install
cp .env.example .env
# fill NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY (names only here; values come from the Supabase dashboard)
bun run dev        # http://localhost:3000
bun run test       # vitest unit tests
bun run types:check
bun run lint:check
bun run build && bun run start   # production build

The repo documents no local Supabase workflow: config.toml holds local defaults (API 54321, DB 54322, Studio 54323, Inbucket 54324) but backend-setup.md states the project does not use the local CLI, so the app is expected to point at a hosted Supabase project.

Auth flow (for test setup)

  1. Login: the browser client calls supabase.auth.signInWithPassword (email and password, plus captchaToken when Turnstile is on) against the Supabase Auth endpoint /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password. It is not a request to the Next.js app, and there is no /api/auth/login.
  2. Session storage: @supabase/ssr writes the session into sb-<project-ref>-auth-token cookies (possibly chunked), sameSite: lax, httpOnly deliberately off, secure only in production.
  3. Gate: middleware.ts runs on every non-asset request, revalidates the user with auth.getUser(), redirects anonymous users from /inicio, /cuenta, /empresas, /dashboard to /login?redirect=... and signed-in users away from /login, /signup, /forgot-password to /inicio. /reset-password is deliberately not redirected.
  4. Email and OAuth entry points: /auth/confirm (OTP token hash via verifyOtp, reads next) and /auth/callback (Google, exchangeCodeForSession, failure goes to /login?error=google-auth-failed).
  5. Sign-out: Server Action salir() in src/app/auth/actions.ts calls auth.signOut(), deletes the empresa_activa_id cookie and redirects to /login.
  6. Active company: cookie empresa_activa_id (set when a company is chosen in /empresas); resolverEmpresaActiva falls back to the most recently created company when the cookie is absent or foreign.

QA relevance: a test account is created through /signup (email confirmation, Turnstile and Google are the obstacles) or the Supabase Admin API; there is no seed data and no test-only login. See discovery-gaps.

Test IDs strategy

data-testid appears 29 times in 6 files (src/app/page.tsx, src/app/signup/page.tsx, dashboard-client.tsx, declaracion-detalle-client.tsx, revision-1376-client.tsx, importar-asiento-dialog.tsx). Values are snake_case, prefixed by feature (importar_asiento_*, revision_1376_*, declaracion_*, borrar_periodo_*, signup_plan_elegido), and mostly mark banners, errors and totals. Three patterns are dynamic templates: periodo_${periodo}, borrar_periodo_${periodo}, plan_${id}. Forms, inputs and buttons carry no test ID, so tests must fall back to role, label and text (the UI is in Spanish) for those. There is no convention document.

Cloud services and database infrastructure

  • Services: Render (web hosting), Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Edge Functions), Resend (email), Cloudflare Turnstile (CAPTCHA), Google (OAuth), BCU (public exchange-rate web service). Details in external services.
  • Database: Supabase-managed PostgreSQL; the region, backup and point-in-time-recovery settings, pooler and connection strings are not in the repo. .env.example has POSTGRES_* names for a direct connection (pooled and non-pooling), used by tooling such as the QA database MCP, not by the app.
  • Monitoring and observability: none (no Sentry, APM, uptime check, log shipping or health endpoint); only Render's own service logs and Supabase dashboard logs, whose retention is unknown.
  • Rollback: not documented. The mechanisms implied by the platform (redeploying a previous commit on Render; no down-migrations in supabase/migrations/, which are forward-only) are not described in any doc.

QA relevance: staging is the default QA target (testing.default_env); its database is shared state with no documented reset, seed or isolation beyond RLS per account.

CI/CD

There is no CI pipeline. The target repo has no .github/workflows, .gitlab-ci.yml, Jenkinsfile, Dockerfile or infrastructure-as-code files. Checks run on the developer's machine through Husky hooks; deployment is performed by the hosting platform.

Husky hooks (installed by prepare: husky)

HookRuns
pre-commitbunx lint-staged (eslint --fix on staged ts, tsx, js, jsx; prettier on staged json, yml, yaml, css, scss, html), bun run types:check, bun run vars:check, bun run skills:check, and skills:registry:check only when skill files are staged
pre-pushbun run format:check && bun run lint:check && bun run vars:env:check && bun run skills:registry:check

Neither hook runs bun run test (Vitest) or bun run build, and hooks can be skipped with --no-verify. vars:* and skills:* belong to the boilerplate tooling. The aggregate repo:check script also omits the unit tests. So nothing enforces that the 20 Vitest files pass before a merge or a deploy.

Discovery gaps

  • API contract source: no OpenAPI spec exists (no openapi.*, swagger.*, or generator package in package.json) and there is no src/app/api; the only route handlers are /auth/callback and /auth/confirm. bun run api:sync has nothing to sync. Next step: /project-context api for the business-angle map (Server Actions, route handlers, PostgREST/RPC surface). Also recorded in .context/project-config.md.
  • Hosted Supabase configuration is not in the repo: supabase/config.toml holds local defaults only (email confirmations off, minimum password 6, no active Send Email hook, CAPTCHA and Google blocks commented or default). Whether the hosted project enables the hook, confirmations, CAPTCHA, the password policy, Google, redirect URLs and max_rows cannot be verified without dashboard or Management API access. The database MCP (dbhub) is not connected, so the live schema and policies were not compared with the migrations.
  • Email delivery state is contradictory: ADR-0002 implements Resend through the hook with the sandbox sender onboarding@resend.dev and no verified domain; the threat model (2026-10-18) still lists the built-in mailer limit of 2 emails per hour and "own SMTP" as pending. Which one is live on staging decides whether a QA mailbox can receive signup and recovery links.
  • Suspected recovery-link defect (unverified): the Edge Function builds /auth/confirm?token_hash=...&type=...&redirect_to=... but /auth/confirm reads next, not redirect_to, so a recovery link may land on /inicio instead of /reset-password. Confirm on staging before treating it as a bug.
  • Turnstile on staging: NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY is not among the variables in render.yaml. Whether staging runs with CAPTCHA decides how login can be automated.
  • Environment variables vs code: render.yaml declares SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY and SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET, which no file in src/ reads. The target .env.example is the boilerplate's own and lists none of the app variables, although env.ts tells developers to copy it.
  • Production host unconfirmed: vercel.json and the SRS say Vercel; render.yaml and staging say Render (also in .context/project-config.md).
  • Possible truncation of declaration data: see NFR-PERF-004; the hosted PostgREST row cap and a real large-file run are unverified.
  • No measured NFR numbers: the 5-minute flow target (NFR-PERF-001) has no timing evidence; no load or performance tests exist; no availability SLA is defined (PRD marks it pending).
  • Observability not implemented: no APM, error tracking, metrics, tracing, log shipping or health endpoint. Only console.error and the error-boundary digest exist. An .env.sentry-build-plugin file sits in the target root and was not opened; no Sentry package is declared. Recommend adding error tracking and a health endpoint.
  • Compliance Needs Review: encryption at rest, data retention for uploaded and generated files, and Uruguayan data-protection requirements are undefined in SRS/12-security.md and have no code evidence.
  • Stale product documents: .context/api-auth.md says signup is pending and that the secret key is never imported in src/ (now used by admin.ts); SRS 02 lists folders and Vercel hosting that the code does not match. Treated as intent, not fact. .context/project-config.md lists 4 RPCs; the migrations define 5 (borrar_periodo added 2026-10-14).
  • Test-architecture ADRs: none written. Vitest as the unit runner is app-internal and the QA suite does not depend on it (fails the architectural gate for the QA suite). data-testid appears 23 times, 22 distinct snake_case values in 7 files, all on status banners and alerts: a partial habit, not a selector contract anyone decided. No code decides test-data isolation or auth-in-tests. Open decisions for /test-framework-adaptation: how tests authenticate given Turnstile, email confirmation and Google OAuth with no seed users, and how test data is isolated per cuenta (RLS gives a natural per-account boundary).
  • Diagram: one architecture figure drawn with diagram-design (default skin, no profile marker). No sequence figure for the auth flow; the numbered steps carry it. Cloudflare Turnstile is described in text only, to stay within the node budget.
  • Phase 3 added: the backend, frontend, environments and ci-cd sections now exist (items below were found while writing them).
  • No CI and no automated test gate: the target has no .github/workflows; Husky hooks run lint, format and types but never bun run test or bun run build, and Render builds without tests. Whether branch protection or required reviews exist on GitHub is not verifiable from the repo.
  • Migration deployment path undocumented: 27 forward-only migrations, no script or pipeline applies them; backend-setup.md says they go through the Supabase MCP and that the local CLI is not used, yet supabase/config.toml and a seed.sql reference exist (the file does not). Order of code deploy versus migration, and whether staging and production share one Supabase project, are unknown.
  • Rollback, backups and monitoring unknown: no rollback procedure, no down-migrations, no documented database backup or point-in-time recovery settings, no error tracking or uptime check.
  • Staging URL mismatch: .context/deploy/render/README.md records tudeclaracion-staging.onrender.com, while .agents/project.yaml uses tudeclaracion-staging-pus8.onrender.com. Render may append a suffix when a name is taken; confirm which URL is live. The README also still calls Render "Plan B" while staging runs on it.
  • Staging build-time configuration unknown: NEXT_PUBLIC_* values are inlined at build, render.yaml omits NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, and SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET is not in the target .env.example. A wrong NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL silently falls back to localhost in email links.
  • Correction to the environment-variables gap above: the target .env.example does list the app variables (NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY) inside a larger boilerplate file; the real gap is that it does not list SEND_EMAIL_HOOK_SECRET and mixes tooling variables with app variables.
  • Test-ID count restated: the scan for this phase found 29 data-testid occurrences in 6 files, not 23 in 7 as in the test-architecture item above (three of them are dynamic templates). The conclusion is unchanged: banners and alerts only, no inputs or buttons.
  • Playwright declared, unused in the app repo: playwright is a dev dependency but no config or spec exists; no accessibility, performance or bundle-size tooling exists, and no not-found, sitemap or robots files.
